topic: The Magic of Roots of Unity: Using Complex Numbers in Combinatorics
target_audience: University students majoring in Mathematics or Computer Science

sections.title: The Root Problem: Filtering Coefficients
lecture_lines: Challenge: Summing every k-th coefficient of P(x).
Use roots of unity as a filter.
Roots vanish when powers aren't multiples of k.
animations: Display a sequence of coefficients a_0, a_1,..., a_n on screen. (#FFFFFF)
Highlight every k-th coefficient (a_0, a_k, a_2k,...) using a flashing orange effect. (#FF5733)
Display the summation formula for the roots of unity filter. (#FF33A8)

sections.title: The Roots of Unity Filter Lemma
lecture_lines: Consider the n-th roots of unity.
Sum their powers: 1/n times the sum.
Cancel all terms except where n divides k.
animations: Draw the unit circle and plot the n-th roots of unity. (#00FF00)
Animate a vector summation of the roots of unity. (#FFFF00)
Display the lemma formula showing cancellation for k not divisible by n. (#FF00FF)

sections.title: Step-by-Step Implementation
lecture_lines: Sum values and divide by n.
animations: Write the generating function P(x) = sum a_i * x^i. (#FFFFFF)
Show P(x) evaluated at each root of unity on the complex plane. (#00FFFF)
Display the final average calculation: (1/n) * sum P(w^j). (#00FF00)

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: Complex filters solve combinatorial problems easily.
Visual intuition leads to algebraic solutions.
